messages:
Tyler (AE): Hey team — heads up on a mid-market POC that needs special pricing + fast deal-desk turnaround. Customer wants a 60-day POC, 3-seat sandbox, and a one-time 20% discount on hosted API for the POC period. Also asking for a short SLA for uptime during the POC. Can we route this for approval?
Alex M: @Tyler (AE) send the SFDC opp id and expected ARR. For deal-desk flow use the 'deal_desk_v2' process — fields we need: deal_desk_status, approval_tier, commit_level, expedite_flag, expedite_reason.
Tyler (AE): opp 0063A00000XyZ12, expected ARR = $42k (annualized if they convert after POC). POC revenue = $3k.
DealDesk Bot: Reminder: standard SLA for review is 48 hours. Mark expedite_flag=true to request 24h review; manager approval required for any expedite. See /deal-desk/templates for expedite justification format.
Alex M: CPQ mapping (paste):
```
- quote.custom.fields.deal_desk_status -> dropdown: pending|approved|rejected
- quote.custom.fields.approval_tier -> picklist: standard|legal-review|required-exec
- quote.custom.fields.commit_level -> picklist: none|monthly|annual
- quote.custom.fields.expedite_flag -> boolean
- quote.custom.fields.expedite_reason -> text
- product.sku -> REDWOOD-POC-SANDBOX
- pricebook.entry -> POCPRICE_20OFF
```
Alex M: For this size we usually route to Tier 1 (standard) unless legal terms are modified. The 20% one-time discount can be approved at Tier 1 if it's only for the POC and ARR < $50k.
Maria P: Quick note on terms — if customer asks to add a data residency or IP clause we need legal review. Security questionnaire (VendorSec) outstanding? That blocks private deployments and some contractual SLAs.
Tyler (AE): VendorSec sent last week, they filled the doc but left the encryption and logging answers blank. They want our standard POC SLA: 99.5% uptime during POC window. Is that acceptable as a short-term SLA?
Samir R: 99.5% for hosted POC is okay but call it a 'POC availability objective' not a formal long-term SLA. Finance: confirm there's a one-time non-recurring charge (POC fee) in the quote for $3k and no automatic renewal. Add a note in quote.comments: 'POC one-time fee, conversion to paid contract requires new quote.'
Alex M: Routing steps I recommend:
1) Create quote in SFDC with the custom fields filled.
2) Attach VendorSec PDF and mark security_docs_attached=true.
3) If expedite_flag=true, set approval_tier=standard and add manager@ops to approvers.
4) If legal changes required, set approval_tier=legal-review and attach redlined terms.
If everything matches, we can get Tier 1 approval in ~24-48h, expedite can get 12-24h depending on manager availability.
Maria P: For the POC SLA wording use this snippet in contract: 'Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 99.5% availability for hosted POC environments during the POC term. This is an availability objective and not an ongoing contractual SLA beyond the POC term.'
Tyler (AE): Perfect — I'll update the quote and set expedite_flag=true (customer pressed for approval this week). Adding manager note now.
DealDesk Bot: Approved routing created: routing_id=RD-2026-789. Assigned approver: Alex M. Deadline: 2026-08-09T18:00:00Z (~24h).
Samir R: FYI — if the customer later requests reserved capacity or dedicated instances during POC, we need a separate capacity commit and finance sign-off. That will change discount approvals.
Alex M: Tyler — when you submit, include: opp id, ARR, POC fee line item, VendorSec attachment, requested availability objective, and shortlist of approvers. That keeps routing smooth.
Tyler (AE): Got it, sending now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Maria P: :eyes: will spot-check legal language when the record is up.
Alex M: once approved I'll post the approval email thread here for audit.
